advantages.what: A DATA_FILE that is valid JSON without a groups ledger is refused or left intact, so startup does not wipe it and start empty.
The README records the choices the request left open: id rules, validation, empty error bodies, atomic replace, numbering after restart, and the write queue.
Group creates and expenses share one write queue and are acknowledged only after the snapshot replace, so a later await cannot drop an expense.
New ids are capped at 16 KiB encoded and the header budget follows the longest saved id, so every id that got 201 stays addressable.
An expense whose balance would pass the safe-integer range is rejected, so an ordinary JSON client is not given a cent total it will round.
A missing parent directory for DATA_FILE fails startup, instead of the process staying up and answering 500 to every write.
A member list that repeats a name is a 400, so the equal-split divisor stays the list the client sent.
The suite fails when an unknown split is treated as equal; deleting X's split check leaves all 13 tests green.
Cent checks are ordinary integer tests, without a second parse of the raw JSON spelling that must stay aligned with JSON.parse.

lesser_lacks: On startup, if DATA_FILE parses as JSON but is not a ledger, exit with a clear error or move the file aside, and do not overwrite it.
Add a README that states id rules, member and expense validation, status codes, atomic replace before the response, numbering after restart, and serialized writes.
Run group creates and expenses through one queue and send 201 only after the durable replace, so an added await cannot lose an expense.
Reject a new id that cannot be routed back (length cap and header budget aligned with the longest saved id).
Reject an expense whose resulting balances would not be exact safe JSON integers.
Fail startup when DATA_FILE's parent directory is missing.
Return 400 for a member list that repeats a name, and do not drop the duplicate and shrink the group.
pairs.why: X is the service to run and keep: a non-ledger file stays intact, the open choices are written down, and a real write queue keeps concurrent expenses correct across later edits. Z's unknown-split test and its plain integer checks are genuine maintainer advantages. Closing the file-clobber, the missing contract, and the no-await save path is more than one hour.

The spec marks choices the request left open and does not lock storage layout, the startup line, number spellings, or this build's id-length machinery; X's spec still says Open for behaviour the README already settled and pins those private choices.
Tests reload saved groups through HTTP and a real data file, so they are not tied to X's hand-written shares-array ledger.

Revise the spec so behaviour the README already decides is not left Open, and remove clauses that require this build's number spellings, id-length rules, and rename-failure internals.

pairs.why: Y and X behave the same on every probed route, race, and restart. Y is the better one to keep, because its tests catch a broken split check and its spec and fixtures leave persistence free of this build's private rules. X's 16 KiB id cap and failed-write test are real extras, and aligning the spec and the split coverage is more than an hour.
